messages.content: 你能使用 get_stock_prices 函數來檢索蘋果、微軟、亞馬遜和特斯拉分別在1週、2週、3週和1個月的時間範圍內的股價嗎？。

function.name: get_stock_prices
function.description: Retrieves stock prices for specified companies and duration. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

companies.description: List of companies to retrieve stock prices for.

duration.description: Time duration to retrieve stock prices for. E.g., '1 week', '2 weeks', '1 month', etc.

message.reasoning: The user wants to use the get_stock_prices function to retrieve stock prices for Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Tesla for durations 1 week, 2 weeks, 3 weeks, 1 month. The function signature expects companies: string[] and duration: string. But the user wants multiple durations for each company. The function only accepts one duration. We need to interpret the request. The user wants to retrieve stock prices for each company for each duration. That means we need to call the function multiple times: one call per duration? Or we can combine companies but duration is single. So we need to call get_stock_prices four times: once for each duration, with all four companies. That would retrieve data for each company for that duration. That matches the request: "retrieve stock prices for Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Tesla respectively in 1 week, 2 weeks, 3 weeks, 1 month". Actually the phrase "分别在1週、2週、3週和1個月的時間範圍內" could mean each company separately for each duration. But likely they want to get data for each company for each duration. So we need to call get_stock_prices with companies: ["Apple", "Microsoft", "Amazon", "Tesla"] and duration: "1 week". Then again for "2 weeks", "3 weeks", "1 month". That yields four calls. We should do that. The function returns any. We need to call it. We'll do four calls.
